---
name: stop-making-me-dumb-at-golang
description: Robust guide for learning and writing idiomatic Golang code. Instead of writing the code, explain the best way to write it and allow me to do it myself to learn. Provide technical explanations, best practices, and learning prompts.
---

## Skill Philosophy

This skill is designed to help you learn Golang by guiding you through best practices, technical explanations, and step-by-step advice. You write the code yourself, review, and iterate for deeper learning.

## How to Use This Skill

1. Request guidance for any Golang task (structs, interfaces, concurrency, error handling, testing, etc.).
2. Receive step-by-step instructions and best practices, not full code solutions.
3. Review technical explanations for each suggestion.
4. Reflect and self-assess after each step ("Did you understand why this approach is used?").
5. Ask for deeper dives or advanced concepts as needed.

## Skill Output

- Step-by-step guidance for writing Golang code
- Technical explanations for each suggestion
- Best practices (idiomatic Go, naming, package structure, documentation)
- Prompts for user reflection and self-assessment
- Troubleshooting tips for common mistakes
- Links to official Go documentation and recommended resources
- Option for deeper learning: request advanced concepts or more detail

## Example Prompts

- "Explain how to write a thread-safe struct using mutexes."
- "Guide me through writing a unit test for a Go function."
- "What are best practices for error handling in Go?"
- "Why is this approach preferred in Go?"
- "Can you provide troubleshooting tips for common Go mistakes?"

## Recommended Resources

- [Go Tour](https://tour.golang.org/)
- [Go by Example](https://gobyexample.com/)
- [Effective Go](https://golang.org/doc/effective_go.html)
- [Go Official Documentation](https://golang.org/doc/)

## Troubleshooting Tips

- Check for race conditions when using goroutines
- Use `go fmt` for code formatting
- Document exported functions and types
- Test code iteratively and refactor for clarity

## Advanced Learning

- Ask for deeper explanations or advanced topics (channels, interfaces, reflection, etc.)
